subject: Re: load_all seems to cause problem with S4 method selection table

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: load_all seems to cause problem with S4 method selection table
parts:
Hi Mark,

I think it's the same basic problem as
https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/60 - the fix is rather
challenging because S4 methods are fundamentally not designed to be
loaded in this way. As far as I can tell, the easiest fix is run to
each test/document command in a completely fresh instance of R - this
will make things a bit slower, but hopefully also more reliable.

Hadley

On Mon, Jun 18, 2012 at 9:11 AM, Mark Hochguertel <mark...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> Am running into problems with using inherited S4 classes with devtools.
> Method selection table seems to stuff up after I use "load_all".
>
> I've managed to track the problem down in the "as" function as described
> after the example script.
>
> I'm running R 2.15.0 on windows (I know, I know, I should be using
> Linux/Mac). I also usually run through Eclipse IDE, but have tried just
> through R and have the same issues.
> Output from sessioninfo() at the end of the message.
>
> Attached is the very simple package file.
>
> ### Start Example ###
>
> # requires
> library(devtools)
> library(roxygen2)
> # I typically run from within dev mode, but happens either way.
> dev_mode()
>
> # testing
> test("Temp")
>
> #create a Child
> child <- new("Child", name = "bob")
>
> #try as
> as(child, "Parent")
> # works fine
>
> # now reload package
> load_all("Temp", TRUE)
> as(child, "Parent")
> # Error in .setupMethodsTables(fdef, initialize = TRUE) :
> # trying to get slot "group" from an object of a basic class ("NULL") with
> no slots
>
> ### End Example ###
>
> What I've managed to decipher is as follows:
>
> The error is being generated from the call on line 10 in function "as":
> coerceMethods <- .getMethodsTable(coerceFun, environment(coerceFun),
> inherited = TRUE)
>
> which subsequently calls ".setupMethodsTables".
>
> Just prior to this (on line 9) of the function "as" is this:
> coerceFun <- getGeneric("coerce", where = where)
>
> When the error is being produced, this line returns NULL instead of the
> "coerce" function as it does normally.
>
> The only variable is "where" (an environment object) , but when I print or
> query with str() from a working or failing condition in a browser call, they
> show up as the same. I also tried digging through "getGeneric" to understand
> what was happening but was quickly swimming in calls to C code.
>
> I'm certainly not an R guru, so I've pretty much come up against the limit
> of my capabilities to resolve. Would appreciate if someone with more brain
> power could take a look.
>
> I hope the above information explains with the appropriate amount of detail.
> Let me know if there is anything else that could be useful.
>
> Cheers,
> Mark.
>
> P.S. devtools and testthat rock! :)
>
>
